doc.name: pwned.coffee
doc.instructions: pwned.coffee: live security incidents with patch status and fixed versions, updated hourly. Not security advice: confirm against the vendor advisory linked on each incident.

tools.name: todays_specials
tools.title: Today's specials
tools.description: Live security incidents right now (CVEs, breaches, supply-chain compromises) with severity, patch status, fixed versions and ids. Pass stack ids to see only what touches your stack. Known ids: nextjs, react, node, bun, php, python, ruby, go, java, wordpress, drupal, magento, perl, proof-tools, dotnet, rust, npm, pypi, github-actions, docker, vscode, browser-ext, linux, linux-services, openssh, nginx, apache, kubernetes, postgres, mysql, redis, gitlab, ci, atlassian, self-hosted, selfhost-apps, paas, cloudflare, aws, gcp, azure, vps, databases-cloud, ai-gateways, ai-keys, ml-infra, mcp, chrome, apple, android, windows, office, office-suites, password-managers, messaging, crypto-wallets, vpn-edge, ics, remote-support, vmware, security-tools, health-it, erp.

stack.description: Stack ids to filter by, e.g. ["nextjs","npm"]. Omit for everything.

tools.name: lookup_cve
tools.title: Look up a CVE
tools.description: The incident covering a CVE or GHSA id, or a named bug (e.g. HTTP2Shell): summary, severity, patch status, fixed versions, timeline and sources.

tools.name: check_lockfile
tools.title: Check a lockfile
tools.description: Match the packages and versions in a lockfile against incidents that state fixed versions, and print a receipt: what you use, the version, affected or not, and the exact upgrade. Accepts package-lock.json, yarn.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml, requirements.txt, poetry.lock, uv.lock, Pipfile.lock, composer.lock, go.sum, go.mod, Cargo.lock, Gemfile.lock, a Dockerfile, an .nvmrc / .node-version ("node") or a GitHub Actions workflow ("actions"). For several files at once, use check_repo.

ecosystem.description: Which reader to use. "auto" detects from the content. "node" is an .nvmrc or .node-version file, "actions" a GitHub Actions workflow.

tools.name: check_repo
tools.title: Check a whole repo
tools.description: Send the files that describe what a project runs (lockfiles, Dockerfiles, .github/workflows/*.yml, wrangler.toml, vercel.json, next.config.*, compose files) in one call. Returns one receipt: every affected package with the exact command to fix it in the tool the repo already uses, actions and images to check, and live incidents for the detected stack that the files cannot rule out.

files.description: Up to 40 files. Paths matter: they pick the reader and the fix command.

tools.name: whats_new
tools.title: What's new since
tools.description: Incidents created or updated since a point in time, newest first. Use it to re-check only what changed since your last run. Accepts "24h", "7d", "90m" or an ISO timestamp.

stack.description: Optional stack ids to filter by.

tools.name: diff_since
tools.title: What changed since, with sources
tools.description: Every correction, new ticket and fix-status change since a point in time, each with the source behind it (the same log as /corrections). Use it to audit what the board changed since your last run. Accepts an ISO 8601 timestamp, or "24h", "7d", "90m".

stack.description: Optional stack ids to filter by.

prompts.name: protect_my_repo
prompts.title: Check this repo against today's specials
prompts.description: Reads the lockfiles, Dockerfiles, workflows and deploy configs, sends them to check_repo, and proposes the upgrades as a diff without applying them.

prompts.name: morning_check
prompts.title: What changed overnight
prompts.description: Calls whats_new for the last 24 hours, filtered to the stack this repo uses, and says whether anything needs doing today.
